newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ashton sees jewellery market recovery.
newsitem.headline: Ashton sees jewellery market recovery.

text.p: Diamond producer Ashton Mining Ltd said on Tuesday that it would continue with its independent marketing strategy in calendar 1997 and forecast growth in the retail jewellery sector after a static 1996.

Ashton chairman Nobby Clark told shareholders at the annual general meeting that the company, which split from the De Beer -operated Central Selling Organisation sales and marketing group in mid-1996, believed the world diamond market should grow in 1997.
Clark said, however, that Ashton's output was expected to fall to 36 million carats in 1997 from 42 million in 1996.
"World retail diamond jewellery sales were static in 1996, with continuing strong growth in the U.S. and much of Asia, offset by a disappointing year in Japan," Clark said.
In notes to be delivered to the meeting, the company said that this year it expected "growth in international retail jewellery sales, particularly in the U.S."

Ashton operates the 40.1 percent owned Argyle opencut diamond mine in Western Australia, with the remainder owned by mining house RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd. Ashton is 46.95 percent owned by Malaysian Mining Corp Bhd.
The chairman did not forecast 1997 profits.

Ashton reported net profits of A$20.57 million in calendar 1996 from A$16.76 million in 1995. Sales were A$181.5 million in the latest year, with managing director John Robinson predicting in March this year that 1997 sales should be higher.

Clark said that this year the company would decide whether to develop Argyle as an underground operation and would also make a decision mid-year about whether to proceed with the development of the Merlin diamond project in Australia's outback Northern Territory.
He said mine production could be underway at Merlin by the 1998 second half if the feasibility study was satisfactory.
Ashton shares were steady at A$1.97 at 11.00 a.m. (0100 GMT) on Tuesday.
